GD PROFILER
Product catalog summary
Introduction
The document emphasizes the significance of understanding the chemical composition of materials, particularly in applications like coated steels and semiconductor wafers. It highlights the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of RF Glow Discharge Optical Emission Spectrometry (RF-GD-OES) for both surface and bulk composition analysis.
Specifications
The GD-Profiler HR features a 1.0m focal length with an optical resolution of 14pm, capable of analyzing up to 60 channels simultaneously. The GD-Profiler 2 includes a 0.5m polychromator for determining up to 47 elements, with an optical resolution ranging from 18 to 25 pm.
Features
- High Dynamic Detectors (HDD™) for enhanced speed and sensitivity.
- CenterLite Laser Alignment System for accurate sample positioning.
- Class E RF generator for stable and real surface analysis.
- Monochromator option for increased flexibility and full spectrum acquisition.
Applications
The GD-Profiler Series is versatile, suitable for thin films, PVD/CVD coatings, semiconductors, and metal alloys, supporting both bulk and compositional depth profile (CDP) analysis.
Performance
The instruments offer high sensitivity and rapid response, with a dynamic range of 1010. The HDD system enables trace element detection with short integration times, improving analysis of complex coatings and multilayer systems.
Software
Quantum XP software provides multitasking capabilities, including Intelligent Quantification (IQ) for precise compositional depth profiles and TimePlus for extended measurement times.
Recognition
The GD-Profiler Series is recognized by ISO Technical Committee TC 201 and has received the NASA Excellence Award, indicating its high quality and reliability.
Additional Insights
RF-GD-OES offers faster analysis times compared to traditional techniques, with the ability to analyze non-conductors without surface charging effects. It measures all elements in one shot, including hydrogen, oxygen, and chlorine, with nanometer-range depth resolution. The technique complements others that provide imaging or molecular information.
Support and Services
Horiba offers comprehensive support, including training, applications assistance, and a range of supplies and upgrades. They provide partnership agreements for service maintenance and facilitate communication through user group meetings and a global network.
Contact Information
Contact details for Horiba offices in France, USA, Japan, Germany, Italy, UK, and China are available for further inquiries and support.

The double pumping system of the HJY RF lamp minimizes the redeposition on the edges of the crater. This allows analysis down to 150 microns with excellent flatness, which is critical for depth resolution.
GD-Profiler Series RF-GD-OES system combines a glow discharge powered by a radio frequency (RF) source with an optical emission spectrometer. Speed and Sensitivity without Compromise for any Application Depth profile analysis is a continuous process of sputtering through a sample at a rate of typically 3 microns per minute. At such a speed, two parameters are critical. First and foremost is time. Valuable information is lost with any time spent waiting or integrating. Second is the ability to respond accurately and immediately to the rapidly changing concentrations as you work through different layers and arrive at various interfaces. This means the ability to measure elements at both trace and major concentrations instantaneously.... Open the catalog to page 4

It is loaded with features like IQ , Intelligent Quantification, that takes the mystery out of the math behind producing accurate Compositional Depth Profiles, TimePlus that allows one to increase the measurement time during a depth profile acquisition and the powerful Quantum Tabler that organizes your valuable data and presents them in easily customizable formats.

RF Glow Discharge Optical Emission Spectrometry for Surface and Thin Film Analysis 7nm
The capability of RF-GD-OES as a tool in surface science is now recognized. Though the technique does not provide lateral resolution, its speed and its ease of use make it the technique of choice for many investigations. Recent examples on hard disks, PZT layers, multilayers on glasses and thin oxides on metals have been published widely. For all these applications, the low energy of the incident particles in RF GD (50eV) assures minimal surface damage.
